title: Review: Transcription; Translation; Protein secretion and the endomembrane system; Oxidative phosphorylation and chemiosmosis
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RS03a#t3 term and clue written for the game; GE05a#t3 term and clue written for the game; CE03#t4 term and clue written for the game; CE03#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: GE04a#N.11, GE05a#N.7, RS03a#N.7a, GE04a#N.5, GE05a#N.10, RS03a#N.10a, GE04a#N.3a, GE05a#N.4, RS03a#N.3a, RS03a#N.5a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: ATP synthase
items.clue: Channel protein in the inner membrane; H⁺ flowing through it turn part of the enzyme.

items.label: Anticodon
items.clue: Three bases on one loop of a clover-leaf molecule, complementary to a triplet on mRNA.

items.label: Pulse-chase
items.clue: Method giving cells radioactive amino acids for a few minutes, then non-radioactive ones

items.label: Golgi apparatus
items.clue: Receives transport vesicles from the RER, then modifies, sorts and packages their contents

questions.stem: α-Amanitin, a toxin from the death cap mushroom, blocks the RNA polymerase that makes mRNA in eukaryotic cells. It has no effect on DNA polymerase or on ribosomes. Which prediction about liver cells exposed to it is correct?

options.text: DNA replication stops, because the cells can no longer separate their DNA strands.
Translation of mRNA already in the cytoplasm stops at once.
No new mRNA is made, so protein synthesis falls as the existing mRNA is broken down.
The DNA of the cells' genes is damaged, so their base sequences change.

questions.explanation: Without RNA polymerase there is no transcription and no new mRNA. Proteins are made only until the existing mRNA runs out.

questions.stem: An antibiotic stops the ribosome from moving along the mRNA but does not affect the binding of tRNAs or the formation of peptide bonds. What effect will this have on translation of an mRNA?

options.text: Only the first peptide bond forms, since the next codon cannot be moved into place for a tRNA to bind.
Translation is unaffected, because all the tRNAs bind along the mRNA before any peptide bonds are formed.
Translation is unaffected, because each tRNA leaves the ribosome before the next one binds to the mRNA.
The chain still grows, because each tRNA stays attached to its amino acid and the next tRNA simply joins onto it.

questions.stem: A student claims: 'Without oxygen the electron transport chain keeps running; only the formation of water stops.' Which statement correctly evaluates this claim?

options.text: Correct: the chain needs only reduced NAD to keep running, and oxygen is required just to make water.
Incorrect: the chain stops because the Krebs cycle needs oxygen to keep supplying it with reduced NAD.
Incorrect: with no terminal acceptor the final carrier remains reduced and electron flow stops.
Incorrect: the chain stops because without oxygen there is no ATP to power the proton pumps.

questions.stem: During transcription, what holds each RNA nucleotide in position against the DNA template strand while it is being added to the growing RNA?

options.text: Hydrogen bonds between complementary bases, which break again when the RNA is released.
Covalent bonds made by RNA polymerase between the RNA base and the DNA base opposite it.
Hydrogen bonds between identical bases, so the RNA is an exact copy of the template.
Hydrogen bonds between adenine and thymine, since RNA contains the same four bases as DNA.

questions.stem: The coding region of an mRNA, from the first nucleotide of the start codon to the last nucleotide of the stop codon, is 903 nucleotides long. How many amino acids does the polypeptide translated from this region contain?
questions.explanation: 903 ÷ 3 = 301 codons. AUG codes for methionine and the stop codon codes for nothing, so the polypeptide has 301 − 1 = 300 amino acids.

questions.stem: A chemical makes the inner mitochondrial membrane freely permeable to protons. Electron flow and oxygen consumption continue, but ATP synthesis stops. Which statement explains these observations?

options.text: Electrons leak through the membrane instead of reaching oxygen, so no energy arrives at ATP synthase.
Water enters the matrix by osmosis, diluting the ADP and phosphate so that they can no longer be joined together.
Reduced NAD cannot transfer energy directly to ADP, because the leak removes the protons that it needs.
Protons leak back into the matrix without passing through ATP synthase, so no gradient remains to drive ADP phosphorylation.

questions.stem: A section of the DNA template strand of a gene has the base sequence TACGCAT. What is the base sequence of the RNA transcribed from this section?

options.text: UACGCAU
AUGCGUA
UAGCGAU
ATGCGTA

questions.explanation: Each RNA base is complementary to the template base: T→A, A→U, C→G, G→C, giving AUGCGUA.

questions.stem: A cell contains many different kinds of tRNA molecule. What is the role of a tRNA during translation?

options.text: It binds to a codon first and then collects from the cytoplasm whichever amino acid that codon specifies.
It brings a specific amino acid to the ribosome and pairs its anticodon with the matching codon on the mRNA.
It delivers an amino acid and remains bonded to it, becoming part of the finished polypeptide chain.
It carries the mRNA bases that the ribosome converts into the amino acids of the polypeptide.

questions.explanation: Each tRNA carries a specific amino acid and has an anticodon complementary to the codons for that amino acid, so base pairing at the ribosome delivers the amino acid the codon specifies.

questions.stem: How is the proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane generated?

options.text: Energy released as electrons flow along the chain pumps protons from the matrix into the intermembrane space.
Protons are pumped from the intermembrane space into the matrix as electrons flow along the chain of carriers.
Hydrolysis of ATP supplies the energy needed to pump protons across the inner membrane into the intermembrane space.
Electrons themselves are pumped across the inner membrane, leaving the protons behind in the matrix.

questions.explanation: At each transfer from carrier to carrier, energy released is used to move protons out of the matrix, across the inner membrane.

questions.stem: How does ATP synthase couple the proton gradient to the synthesis of ATP?

options.text: It hydrolyses ATP to pump protons across the inner membrane into the intermembrane space, building the gradient.
Protons flow through it down their gradient into the matrix, releasing energy that phosphorylates ADP.
Water moves through it by osmosis into the matrix, and the resulting pressure change forces phosphate onto ADP.
Protons collect in the intermembrane space and phosphorylate ADP there, on the outer surface of the enzyme.

questions.explanation: ATP synthase is the route by which protons diffuse back into the matrix. The energy released is coupled to joining phosphate to ADP: chemiosmosis.
